summary.name: How to write a status page update
summary.one_liner: A Hosted Graphite SRE blog post setting out guidelines for writing customer-facing status page updates during incidents, with examples of titles, message content, tone, and time formatting.
keywords: how to notify customers of outage
use_cases: Writing a status page title that tells users how an incident affects them
Deciding what details to share publicly during an outage
Avoiding empty apologies and blame-shifting in outage messages
Standardising timestamps in UTC for public incident communication
summary.what_it_does: The post is a guide, not a software tool. It describes the elements of a good status page update: a title that states user impact, a message covering impact, unaffected areas (especially data loss), start and resolution times, a technical description, and the mitigation steps. It explains how open to be, suggesting generic service names and percentages rather than absolute counts. It also gives language advice: be specific about monitoring, use active voice, split updates into paragraphs, avoid stock apologies and blaming providers, and use UTC 24h times.
notable: Concrete before/after examples of vague versus specific titles and updates
Guidance on sharing technical detail with an engineer audience without exposing internal names or absolute counts
Explicit rules against empty apologies, blame-shifting to providers, and non-UTC times
caveats: Describes one company's internal guidelines; it is not a general standard
Mentions a status page but does not name a specific status page product beyond links to related reading
